title: U.S. House · California's 23rd Congressional District
area: The High Desert region of San Bernardino County, including Victorville, Apple Valley, Hesperia, and Big Bear Lake.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 elections under Proposition 50, a mid-decade redistricting measure voters approved in a November 2025 special election.
In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Jay Obernolte won 57.1% of the vote (81,346 votes) and Tessa Lynn Hodge won 21.3% (30,292 votes), advancing them both to the November general election.

summary.text: Jay Obernolte is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for California's 23rd District. A video-game developer with degrees in engineering and artificial intelligence, he served on Big Bear Lake local boards, as mayor of Big Bear Lake, and in the California Assembly before being elected to Congress in 2020. He sits on the Energy and Commerce, Science, Space, and Technology, and Budget committees.

background.text: Born in Chicago, Illinois, in 1970, and graduated from Edison High School in 1988.

Earned a bachelor's degree in engineering and applied science from Caltech in 1992, a master's degree in artificial intelligence from UCLA in 1997, and a doctorate in public administration from California Baptist University in 2020. His House biography says he is the only serving member of Congress with a graduate-level degree in AI.
Worked as a video-game developer and owned a video-game development studio.

Served on the Big Bear Lake city council from 2010 to 2014, including as mayor from 2012 to 2014. His House biography also lists service on the Big Bear Lake Fire Protection District board, the Mojave Desert and Mountain Integrated Waste Authority, the Mountain Regional Transit Authority, and the Big Bear City Airport District.
Served in the California State Assembly (33rd District) from 2014 to 2020.
Elected to the U.S. House in November 2020 and took office in 2021; represents California's 23rd District after redistricting.

In the 2025-2026 Congress he serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee (Communications and Technology, Health, and Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade subcommittees), the Budget Committee, and the Science, Space, and Technology Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Research and Technology.
According to his House biography, he lives in Big Bear Lake with his wife Heather and their two sons, and is a certified flight instructor and a martial arts teacher.

priorities.text: A market-based, multimodal approach to energy production will help reduce the price Californians pay for electricity and ensure that families are not forced to choose between turning on the lights and putting food on the table.
It is critical that we work to secure our southern border and stop the flow of illegal immigrants, drugs, and human trafficking into the United States.
I am committed to supporting law and order in our country and working to keep our communities safe.

positions.summary: Supports securing the border and stopping illegal immigration, and has toured ICE detention facilities defending their operations against criticism.
positions.quote: It is critical that we work to secure our southern border and stop the flow of illegal immigrants, drugs, and human trafficking into the United States.

positions.summary: Favors a market-based approach that keeps fossil fuels in the energy mix rather than a faster transition away from them, and has introduced resolutions to roll back California vehicle-emissions mandates.
positions.quote: A market-based, multimodal approach to energy production will help reduce the price Californians pay for electricity and ensure that families are not forced to choose between turning on the lights and putting food on the table.

positions.summary: Opposes defunding law enforcement and supports keeping police departments fully resourced.
positions.quote: defunding law enforcement is certainly not a viable option, and stripping them of their ability to keep us safe is a dangerous path for our nation

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Communications and Technology; Health subcommittees), chairs the Research and Technology Subcommittee of the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and serves on the House Committee on Budget in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Tessa Lynn Hodge
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2 top-two primary with 21.3% of the vote

summary.text: Tessa Lynn Hodge is the Democratic nominee for California's 23rd District. She describes herself as a lifelong High Desert resident and a Licensed Clinical Social Worker with nearly a decade of experience, and says she is running on healthcare, jobs and housing affordability.

background.text: According to her campaign website, she was born and raised in the High Desert and has lived in the district her entire life; her grandfather served 22 years in the Air Force and later ran a print shop in Victorville, and her grandmother worked more than 30 years as a registered nurse, mostly at St. Mary's Medical Center in Apple Valley.

Describes herself as a Licensed Clinical Social Worker with almost a decade of experience working with vulnerable populations, from children in foster care to students needing mental-health services in school districts.
Has worked in San Bernardino County incorporating state and federal legislation into county policy and guidelines for county workers.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, finishing second behind Jay Obernolte with 21.3% of the vote; this is her first campaign for the seat on the Ballotpedia record reviewed.

priorities.text: Names healthcare as a top priority, saying she will fight for Medicare for All while working to expand healthcare services in the district's rural areas.
Supports job creation with 'living wage' careers, including workforce training and small-business investment.
Supports expanding affordable housing and renter protections in the district.

positions.summary: Supports Medicare for All and expanding healthcare services in the district's rural areas.
positions.quote: I will fight for Medicare for all while also working to expand healthcare services in our rural district.

positions.summary: Supports expanding affordable housing and protecting renters.
positions.quote: I will push to expand affordable housing, protect renters, and cut red tape that drives up costs
